text: This is a term that has become very common recently.
Many people complain about it without knowing the cause. They take a supplement, and the level improves somewhat.
Then, after they stop the supplement, the vitamin D level in the blood starts to fall again, and the same symptoms return.
They may complain of pain in the long bones and pain in the lower spine; many people with vitamin D deficiency report these symptoms.
In my view, they need to understand that the underlying problem is in the liver, and the liver should be addressed first.
I believe the liver needs to make good use of the cholesterol that reaches it instead of allowing it to accumulate.
The liver produces cholesterol because the body needs cholesterol for many functions.
Cholesterol has many uses in the body, so the important thing is for the body to use and process it properly.
In my view, before focusing only on the secondary symptoms, vitamin D deficiency can be related to the body not using cholesterol properly.
That is the point I am making here.
